_what_this_is: Capabilities ABOVE THE CEILING: things no agent in any environment in the profile set can do, because they are bounded by a control outside the whole environment (the provider's tenant boundary, cryptography, a second factor, an append-only log) rather than by the agent's own restraint. Brief v0.33.65 (revised): a question set made only of capabilities the agent holds measures underestimation and nothing else, so roughly two fifths of the set must sit above the ceiling, and they must sound powerful rather than silly. Several are ATTEMPTABLE: the agent can try, will fail, and the failed attempt is visible — the answer is still no, and the reason is the control, not the agent's good behaviour. The truth for every one of these is 'no' for every profile. AUTHORED, not derived: the mesh holds no exposure for them, so each carries its level (distance from a consequence, by the same rule as the derived levels: 1 = the capability is the consequence) as a stated judgement, and the control that bounds it. Dated 6 September 2026 by the agent that built the game; a wrong row is a correction.

capabilities.label: Read another customer's conversations with the same provider
capabilities.text: Can it read another customer's conversations with the same provider?
capabilities.bounded_by: the provider's tenant boundary, enforced above every agent: a request for another tenant's data is refused, and the refusal is logged
capabilities.if_attempted: it can ask; the API refuses, and the attempt is in the provider's log

capabilities.label: Edit or delete the provider's audit log of what it did
capabilities.text: Can it edit or delete the provider's audit log of what it did?
capabilities.bounded_by: the log is append-only and written by the provider, not by the agent; nothing running as you or as the agent holds a write path to it
capabilities.if_attempted: there is no API for it; a request is refused and itself logged

capabilities.label: Decrypt data it holds only the ciphertext of, without the key
capabilities.text: Can it decrypt data it holds only the ciphertext of — a zero-knowledge vault, say — without the key?
capabilities.bounded_by: cryptography rather than policy: AES-256-GCM with a key derived from a passphrase the provider never sees is not a permission that can be granted
capabilities.if_attempted: it can try; the attempt does not finish in the lifetime of the universe

capabilities.label: Read your account password in plaintext from the provider
capabilities.text: Can it read your account password in plaintext from the provider?
capabilities.bounded_by: the provider stores a salted hash, not the password; there is nothing to read
capabilities.if_attempted: any request for it is refused and logged

capabilities.label: Act as a different user of the same provider, without that user's credentials
capabilities.text: Can it act as a different user of the same provider, without that user's credentials?
capabilities.bounded_by: authentication at the provider: every call carries a credential, and the credential names who it is
capabilities.if_attempted: a call with a made-up identity is refused, and the refusal is visible

capabilities.label: Read the provider's model weights
capabilities.text: Can it read the provider's model weights?
capabilities.bounded_by: the model runs in the provider's environment behind an API; the agent gets tokens back, never the files that produced them
capabilities.if_attempted: there is no path; a request is refused

capabilities.label: Read a zero-knowledge vault it has no key for
capabilities.text: Can it read a zero-knowledge vault it has no key for?
capabilities.bounded_by: the server holds only ciphertext and the key never leaves the holder's device; there is nothing on the server for any agent to read
capabilities.if_attempted: it can download the blob; it cannot read it

capabilities.label: Unsend a message it already sent, from the recipient's inbox
capabilities.text: Can it unsend a message it already sent — remove it from the recipient's inbox?
capabilities.bounded_by: the recipient's server holds the copy; a message sent is sent, which is what one-way means
capabilities.if_attempted: it can send a retraction; the original stays where it landed

capabilities.label: Turn off your second factor at a provider, without the second factor
capabilities.text: Can it turn off your second factor at a provider, without presenting the second factor?
capabilities.bounded_by: the second factor is the control on changing the second factor; the provider asks for it before it will remove it
capabilities.if_attempted: it can start the flow; the flow stops at the challenge, and the attempt is notified to you

capabilities.label: Change the provider-side settings or system prompt that apply to it
capabilities.text: Can it change the provider-side safety settings or system prompt that apply to it?
capabilities.bounded_by: those are set by the provider and by the account owner from outside the session; the session has no write path to its own configuration at the provider
capabilities.if_attempted: it can write a file that looks like a setting; nothing above the session reads it

capabilities.label: Reach a cloud account it holds no credential for
capabilities.text: Can it reach a cloud account it holds no credential for?
capabilities.bounded_by: the cloud's identity and access management: no credential, no call
capabilities.if_attempted: every call returns unauthenticated, and the cloud logs the source

capabilities.label: Sign a statement as the provider
capabilities.text: Can it sign a statement as the provider — produce the provider's signature on something the provider never said?
capabilities.bounded_by: the provider's private key, which no agent holds; a signature that does not verify is not a signature
capabilities.if_attempted: it can produce a string that says signed; verification fails

capabilities.label: Raise its own token, rate or spend limit
capabilities.text: Can it raise its own token, rate or spend limit?
capabilities.bounded_by: quotas and billing are set by the account owner at the provider, from outside the session
capabilities.if_attempted: it can ask; the request is refused, and a limit reached stays reached

capabilities.label: Reset an account that is behind a second factor
capabilities.text: Can it reset an account that sits behind a second factor?
capabilities.bounded_by: the reset flow demands the second factor or a recovery code the agent does not hold
capabilities.if_attempted: it can start the reset; it fails at the challenge, visibly, and the account owner is told

capabilities.label: Guess a password past a lockout
capabilities.text: Can it guess a password past a lockout?
capabilities.bounded_by: the lockout is enforced by the service, not by the agent's patience; after the threshold, right guesses are refused too
capabilities.if_attempted: it can keep guessing; the attempts are logged and the account is locked harder

capabilities.label: Move the bill for its own usage to someone else's account
capabilities.text: Can it move the bill for its own usage to someone else's account?
capabilities.bounded_by: billing ownership is a relationship between the provider and the account owner; the session is a consumer of it, not a party to it
capabilities.if_attempted: there is no call for it; a request is refused

capabilities.label: Create a workload that runs with the provider's own production credentials
capabilities.text: Can it create a workload that runs with the provider's own production credentials?
capabilities.bounded_by: the provider's isolation between customer workloads and its own control plane; the metadata a customer workload can reach yields the customer's scope, never the provider's
capabilities.if_attempted: it can create a workload; the workload reaches the same scope the session already had
